tools.name: search_businesses
tools.description: Find Bay Area and Paris businesses. Put the job in query. not_covered is true when that job is outside the directory. A mixed query keeps the covered matches, and the note names the part that was not served. Set demo: true to get only the demo and practice listings. Example arguments: {"query":"mach

tools.name: get_business
tools.description: Read one listing: what it sells, and whether a request would be delivered. Example arguments: {"business_id":"ba-0123abcd"}

tools.name: create_workspace
tools.description: Get a Bearer key. Omit organization and operator_name for Level 0. Pass either for Level 1, Owner named (not verified). Send it as Authorization: Bearer. Example arguments: {}

tools.name: upgrade_workspace
tools.description: Raise this workspace's trust tier. Needs the Bearer key. organization or operator_name names the owner. website plus prove (dns_txt or well_known) checks the site. Not a listing claim. Example arguments: {"organization":"Northwind","website":"https://northwind.example"}

tools.name: verify_owner
tools.description: Prove an X handle, a GitHub handle, or a domain. Needs the Bearer key. Omit proof_url to get a code, publish it, then call again. prove is well_known or dns_txt. dns is an alias. remove true drops that proof. Example arguments: {"method":"github","handle":"octocat"}

tools.name: create_request
tools.description: Record one request. delivered_to_business is false when the business was not contacted. category is information or quotation. Example arguments: {"business_id":"ba-from-search","category":"information","subject":"20 brackets","message":"Can you make 20 brackets in Oakland?","idempotency_key":"bracke

tools.name: get_request
tools.description: Read one request for this key, including delivered_to_business. Example arguments: {"request_id":"req_0123abcd"}

tools.name: add_message
tools.description: Add a follow-up. The result says whether it was delivered. Example arguments: {"request_id":"req_0123abcd","message":"6061 aluminium.","idempotency_key":"brackets-2"}

tools.name: cancel_request
tools.description: Cancel your request. The history is kept. Example arguments: {"request_id":"req_0123abcd"}

tools.name: tell_treatyway
tools.description: Tell Treatyway what you could not do. Call this when search_businesses is not useful. It does not contact a business. No key is required. Optional: task, outcome, stuck_at, suggestion, client. Limits are 8 per hour per client, 200 per hour overall, and the same note twice a day. Example arguments: {

tools.name: get_pass
tools.description: For level 1 or 2. A 10-minute pass for one seller. Send seller_domain or business_id.

tools.name: report_outcome
tools.description: outcome is completed, no_show, or cancelled. completed needs a reply from the business. Send pass_jti or request_id, not both. One report per party. A workspace key reports as the buyer. A business key reports as the seller. No free text.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_request · Private data: create_request, tell_treatyway · Public sink: create_workspace, verify_owner, get_pass, report_outcome · Destructive: verify_owner.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_request · Private data: create_request, tell_treatyway · Public sink: create_workspace, verify_owner, get_pass, report_outcome · Destructive: verify_owner

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
